newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Damark expects club membership gains.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Damark expects club membership gains.

text.p: Damark International Inc chief executive officer Mark Cohn said Wednesday he expects the company's club membership to increase 10 to 12 percent in 1997.

"The analysts' expectation for membership growth in 1997 is in the 10 to 12 percent range, and we're comfortable with that," Cohn told Reuters after the annual shareholders' meeting here this morning. "If we continue to see expanded sales from the catalog retail business, then that will give us a little more growth in our membership side as well."
In the first quarter of 1997, the direct marketing and membership services company's club membership grew 10 percent from the same period last year to 1.1 million.
Cohn said Damark may accept narrower gross margins to effect an increase in its sales.
The company has already completed significant changes to its catalog retail business and has already reaped results from those improved efficiencies, Cohn said.

"So I would not expect to see margins continue to grow," he said. "And we may choose to give up a little bit of the margin gain that we've gotten in favor of driving more sales. Any upward revision in earnings (expectations) will result from an increase in sales."

In the first quarter of 1997 and in 1996, Damark had a gross margin of 28 percent, up from 1995's gross margin of 25 percent. Earlier today, Cohn told the shareholders he was "very comfortable" with analysts' expectations for a 25 percent increase in earnings per share in 1997. The company earned $0.70 per share in 1996.
Cohn told the shareholders Damark's long-term growth prospects are tied to its ability to gain access to third party lists of membership prospects.

"If we're going to grow this business in a meaningful way, long-term it is critically important that we provide added value to other third party list owners," Cohn said. "You should demand of us more deals like the Household deal to be brought to market yet this year."
Last week, Damark announced it had signed an agreement with Household Credit Services Inc which would allow Damark to market membership services to some of Household's credit card customers.

When asked to detail his expectations for this agreement, Cohn told the shareholders, "The agreement allows us to test our Vacation Passport travel club into a couple of Household's portfolios. Our goal is to be successful with a return on investment the second year, and we hope to get access to the greater portfolio in relatively short order."
